method.value: 10 000 random sub-sets of 3-25 sources; integrate line-free channels (>2 FWHM) at radii 0.2-3"; rank sources by summed grades; max sub-sample above mean rank

evidence.quote: The sub-sample selection is done by randomly selecting sub-sets of $n$ sources, where $n$ is in the range 3$-$25, and repeated 10 000 times.

claims.hypothesis: Does the full sample of z~6 quasars show a stacked broad [CII] component?
claims.experiment: 1-D and 3-D stacking with three weightings and two-Gaussian fits
claims.result: Excess 0.4-0.7 sigma (1-D) and 1.1-1.5 sigma (3-D); FWHM>700 km/s

claims.finding: Method is unlikely to produce spurious signal

evidence.quote: the probability to falsely detect a broad component with an excess emission of $>0.4\sigma$ is $<$17%.

why_this_method.value: Individual spectra lack sensitivity, so stacking is the only available method

evidence.quote: spectral stacking is the only available method at present to determine the presence of outflow signatures

limitations_admitted.value: Assumes a single broad Gaussian outflow profile; broad emission could be from interacting galaxies; low-velocity outflows not detectable

evidence.quote: we have assumed that the outflow emission signature has the spectral profile of a single broad Gaussian
